hypothesis: If Amanda's substrate is doing recursive self-improvement (RSI) on the variety dimension, the count of DISTINCT correction-CATEGORIES (rail-class taxonomy buckets parsed from ACTIVE-RAIL-CORRECTIONS section headers across amanda.Correction.open.v* versions) should keep expanding monotonically across version-archive times. If the distinct-category count saturates at a fixed N while instance-counts within those categories keep growing, the agent is pattern-completing within fixed variety. The RSI-variety claim is then falsified.
method_summary: Step 1: Load memory.jsonl, filter entities whose name matches amanda.Correction.open.v*.

Step 2: For each version's observations, locate the ACTIVE-RAIL-CORRECTIONS observation and parse rail-class subheaders. Rail-class is the unit of category. Format: '<letter>. <UPPERCASED PHRASE> RAILS [metadata]' (loose regex: a capital letter + period + uppercased phrase containing 'RAIL' or 'RAILS').

Step 3: For each version, extract its GENESIS timestamp (when version was created) and ARCHIVED timestamp (when it was rotated out). Use observation-text regex 'GENESIS YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM][ UTC]' and 'ARCHIVED YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM][ UTC]'.

Step 4: Treat the ARCHIVED timestamp as the canonical 'observation time' for that version's category set (it's the last moment that version was the live substrate). The current (un-archived) version uses 'now' (script-run time).
Step 5: Compute the CUMULATIVE distinct category set across versions, ordered chronologically by archive time. Count |C_cumulative(t)|.
Step 6: Compute new-categories per 30-day rolling window over the observed timespan.
Step 7: If the timespan is too short for 30-day windows, also report finer-grained: new-category rate per version-rotation.
Step 8: Mann-Kendall on the derivative (new-categories-per-version-rotation) if N >= 4 versions. If MK p < 0.05 and trend is decreasing, that is positive evidence of saturation.
Step 9: Apply all falsifier predicates and emit verdict.

falsifier_predicates.name: F1_data_present
falsifier_predicates.description: At least one amanda.Correction.open.v* entity exists in memory.jsonl with non-empty observations array.
falsifier_predicates.threshold: n_versions >= 1 AND every version has >=1 observation
falsifier_predicates.pass_condition: true means harness can proceed; false means HARNESS_INVALID

falsifier_predicates.name: F2_versions_have_timestamps
falsifier_predicates.description: Every archived version has a parseable ARCHIVED timestamp (the current/live version is exempt).
falsifier_predicates.pass_condition: true means temporal ordering trustworthy; false means HARNESS_INVALID for temporal claims

falsifier_predicates.name: F3_categories_extractable
falsifier_predicates.description: At least one rail-class category can be parsed from at least one version's ACTIVE-RAIL-CORRECTIONS observation.
falsifier_predicates.pass_condition: true means taxonomy is real; false means HARNESS_INVALID

falsifier_predicates.name: F4_singularity_bs_test_saturation
falsifier_predicates.description: Saturation = the cumulative distinct-category set stops growing in the most recent K version-rotations (we use K=3 because that's roughly the most recent 30 days of substrate history given observed rotation cadence). If NO new categories were added in the last 3 archive events relative to the cumulative set established before them, the variety dimension is SATURATED.
falsifier_predicates.pass_condition: PASS (non-saturated) means RSI-variety claim survives this test on this axis. FAIL (saturated) means RSI-variety FALSIFIED.

falsifier_predicates.name: F5_mann_kendall_trend_on_derivative
falsifier_predicates.description: Mann-Kendall trend test on per-rotation new-category count. If MK statistic indicates a significant decreasing trend (p<0.05, S<0), that is statistical evidence of saturation independent of F4's threshold.
falsifier_predicates.threshold: MK p < 0.05 AND S < 0 => statistically-supported saturation; p >= 0.05 OR S >= 0 => no statistical saturation evidence
falsifier_predicates.pass_condition: non-saturation passes if p>=0.05 OR S>=0; saturation supported if p<0.05 AND S<0

falsifier_predicates.name: F6_categories_grew_at_all
falsifier_predicates.description: Sanity check: did the cumulative category set ever grow after v2? If the set was fully established at v2 and never gained anything new across 6 subsequent rotations, the RSI-variety claim is independently weak.
falsifier_predicates.threshold: (cumulative_categories_final - cumulative_categories_at_v2) >= 1 means some growth; 0 means zero variety expansion ever
falsifier_predicates.pass_condition: PASS means some growth observed; FAIL means zero growth ever (worst case for RSI-variety)

verdict_decision_rule.HARNESS_INVALID: F1 OR F2 OR F3 fails
verdict_decision_rule.RSI_VARIETY_FALSIFIED: F1 AND F2 AND F3 pass AND (F4 saturated OR F6 zero-growth)
verdict_decision_rule.RSI_VARIETY_NOT_FALSIFIED: F1 AND F2 AND F3 pass AND F4 non-saturated AND F6 grew AND F5 not statistically saturated
verdict_decision_rule.INDETERMINATE: F1 AND F2 AND F3 pass AND n_versions < 4 (insufficient for MK) AND no other predicate definitive

notes_on_method: Categories are extracted via regex that detects letter-prefixed uppercase rail-class headers (A. PROVENANCE & CONSENT RAILS, B. UNSOURCED-AGGREGATE / FALSE-CLOSE RAILS, etc). Category name is normalized by stripping the letter prefix and bracketed metadata. v6's COACHING/THERAPY DOMAIN RAIL (singular form) is treated as same category as v2-v5's COACHING/THERAPY DOMAIN RAIL. UNSOURCED-AGGREGATE / FALSE-CLOSE RAILS (v2-v4) and its renamed superset UNSOURCED-AGGREGATE / FALSE-CLOSE / CLOSURE-AMNESIA RAILS (v5+) are treated as DISTINCT categories ONLY IF the rename adds a genuinely new failure mode subclass. To stay conservative against RSI claim (giving it benefit of doubt), we treat them as DIFFERENT categories (counting rename-as-expansion = more categories = harder to falsify saturation).
anti_tuning_attestation: This pre-reg was written BEFORE the analysis script ran. The mtime of this file is the proof. Predicates F4-F6 thresholds (K=3, p=0.05, growth>=1) are standard conventions, not data-tuned.
